This is CNBC's live coverage of Apple's 2026 third-quarter earnings.

Apple reported stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for the fiscal third quarter, driven by a 22% increase in iPhone sales. But the company issued weak guidance for the current period, citing "supply constraints." The stock slid more than 6% in extended trading.

Here's how the company did versus LSEG consensus estimates:

Here's how Apple did in other key areas:

Net income climbed to $29.79 billion, or $2.02 per share, from $23.43 billion, or $1.57 per share, a year ago. Apple said earnings included 11 cents per share from tariff rebates. [...] The stock was fell 1.4% for the day to close at $333.43. It's the second straight day of slippage after the stock hit a record on Tuesday, when the company briefly crossed the $5 trillion market cap milestone for the first time.

Even with the drop, Apple shares are up about 23% for the year.

— Ari Levy

Apple has topped revenue and earnings estimates for 13 straight quarters, dating back to the period ended December 2022.

When the company last missed expectations, overall sales for the holiday quarter dropped 5%, the first year-over-year decline since 2019.

Cook said at the time that three factors hurt the results: a strong dollar, production issues in China affecting the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 14 Pro Max, and the overall macroeconomic environment. [...] — Kif Leswing

Apple's iPad sales declined 6% on an annual basis. The company blamed the weakness on a difficult comparison to last year's quarter, when sales of the devices surged due to a new low-cost iPad.

Revenue in the company's wearables and home category increased 6% on an annual basis to $4.9 billion, topping estimates.

— Kif Leswing

Apple's services division, which delivers hefty margins, continued its steady growth, posting a revenue increase of 12% during the quarter to over $30 billion, although it missed analyst estimates. Apple said the services performance was hurt by foreign exchange headwinds.

Apple highlighted growth from advertising, App Store, AppleCare warranties, music, video, cloud services, and payment services.

JPMorgan Chase & Co. JPM emphasized organic capital deployment, resilient business activity and cautious risk management during its third-quarter 2026 earnings call. Management also outlined expectations for higher net interest income in 2027 while acknowledging uncertainty surrounding interest rates and economic conditions.

The bank reported adjusted earnings of $5.75 per share, missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $5.94 by 3.2%. Reported revenues of $50.17 billion also fell short of the consensus estimate of $52.21 billion by 3.9%.

### JPMorgan Chase & Co. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise [...] Consumer & Community Banking revenues advanced 9% to $21.2 billion. Debit and credit-card spending increased 10%, while the bank added more than 650,000 net new checking accounts. Management described consumer finances as resilient, supported by employment conditions.

## JPM Weighs Credit Risks Against Growth Opportunities

Credit conditions remained an important focus as analysts questioned the implications of sustained higher borrowing costs.

Responding to a KBW analyst, Dimon indicated that JPMorgan was tightening certain lending standards, citing weaker covenants and aggressive financing structures. Barnum maintained that corporate balance sheets remained generally sound. [...] Dimon reinforced restrictions on external AI agents accessing internal systems. Barnum also acknowledged that productivity benefits from generative AI remain difficult to identify in quarterly financial results, despite encouraging internal experimentation.

## JPMorgan Sees Strong Equities and Consumer Activity

Commercial & Investment Bank revenues increased 14% year over year to $22.7 billion, supported by investment banking, payments and equities activity.

Barnum highlighted a 49% increase in Equity Markets revenues, contrasting with a 4% decline in Fixed Income Markets. Investment banking fees rose 14%, although management noted some moderation in transaction activity amid bond-market volatility.

Lucid's second-quarter results included a net loss of more than $1 billion compared with a loss of $539.4 million during the second quarter of last year. The company reported an adjusted loss of $901.1 million, or $3.30 per share, compared with a loss of $632.1 million, or $2.80 per share, a year earlier.

The losses were on production of 4,774 vehicles, up 24% year over year, and deliveries of 3,953 vehicles, up 19%, during the second quarter. The company currently offers the Air sedan and Gravity SUV that start at roughly $70,000 and $80,000, respectively. [...] They include approximately $600 million to $800 million in vehicle inventory, $500 million in capital expenditures, and $200 million in operating expenses, the company said.

In addition to the cost-cutting, Lucid said the plan will broadly focus on three key areas: "cash and cost," "customer and quality" and "culture and team."

More specifically, the company said its efforts will focus on its robotaxi program with Uber and Nuro; a factory that's under construction in Saudi Arabia; and its upcoming midsize vehicle. Lucid called the robotaxi initiative a "top priority." [...] "Silvio and his leadership team are transforming the company, and the Board stands firmly behind their actions," Lucid Chairman Turqi Alnowaiser said in a release.

The missed results and comments come weeks after Lucid denied an online report that it was considering bankruptcy or taking the company private. The report caused shares of the company to plummet. The stock recovered some of those losses, but remains off nearly 30% in 2026.

Napoli adamantly denied such plans on Tuesday to CNBC, as he did when they were reported.

"I wholeheartedly reinforce the denial," he said. "We are here to stay. We are here. We have a plan. We have a board and a majority investor that will help us to go through what is admittedly a moment where we are doing many things at the same time."
